entries.claim: The inspected NewAPI source declares existing routes for login, refresh, self, user models, top-up, pricing, and session management.
The inspected NewAPI pricing model exposes model ID, input/output/cache ratios, billing mode/expression, enabled groups, endpoint types, and a pricing version.
The inspected NewAPI pricing UI derives token input price from model_ratio multiplied by two and by a selected or available group ratio, then applies output and cache multipliers.

The inspected NewAPI pricing response structure has pricing values and a pricing version but no explicit official-source URL, official verification timestamp, or field declaring that the base value is a vendor official price.

The inspected NewAPI models.dev ratio importer selects the cheapest non-zero provider price for duplicate model names, so imported base ratios are not mechanically guaranteed to be the model vendor's own official price.

Read-only requests to the deployed first-party origins on 2026-08-30 returned system name 野菜API and version v1.0.0-rc.27 from both /api/status endpoints, HTTP 404 for /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap, HTTP 401 for unauthenticated /api/user/self, and a public /api/pricing projection containing 37 models plus pricing_version a42d372ccf0b5dd13ecf71203521f9d2. This verifies current public behavior only and does not establish a deployed desktop authorization or stable desktop pricing projection.

The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

The locally inspected NewAPI upstream snapshot has consumption quota, token fields, model mapping and partial price/rule traces, distinguishes subscription from wallet debit, and its standard usage summary sums consume logs with separate last-minute RPM/TPM. These structures do not prove production deployment parity or a complete historical official-price-versus-net-charge projection.

entries.claim: Anonymous read-only GET of /api/desktop/v1/bootstrap returned HTTP 404 with JSON error envelopes on both approved Yeschoy origins. No credential was sent. Current client account readiness remains backend_upgrade_required. This prevents claiming live account, tool-key or historical billing integration.

Current native config uses default titlebar, appearance hook only styles DOM; discovery treats distinct binaries as conflicts including app-bundled codex. Locked Tauri supports Transparent titlebar and native Window background without custom decorations.

The current build host is Intel macOS with only x86_64-apple-darwin installed. The inherited tag-triggered release workflow publishes broad upstream-named assets and requires updater signing secrets; it is not a safe Windows internal-build path. The private origin can instead run a separate manual Windows 2022 artifact-only workflow without signing, updater, tag or release authority.

The current official NewAPI GitHub HEAD 918427d8ab41f6adaa4113d0496f1f8621855b70 exposes browser login, refresh-cookie, current-user, pricing, usage-log, and top-up routes, but no /api/desktop/v1 device-authorization boundary. Its documented browser session keeps a 15-minute access token in browser memory and a rotating HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie, so it is not a safe drop-in desktop-device credential contract.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

Anonymous read-only inspection shows both approved Yeschoy origins report NewAPI v1.0.0-rc.27, the public pricing route responds, and the proposed desktop bootstrap route is absent. That exact official NewAPI tag already persists revocable user sessions through AutoMigrate and records applied model, group, completion, cache and fixed-price billing inputs in consumption log Other data. Therefore a desktop device authorization adapter can reuse existing business tables and user_sessions, with only short-lived authorization state in Redis; immutable official-price provenance can be added to existing option/log JSON without a schema change.

RU-002 should preserve the verified RU-001 discovery experience and add a client-only account and billing shell whose sole runtime account projection is backend_upgrade_required. It must show no fabricated account, balance, usage, price, authorization, or wallet result and must make no production account request until a later frozen unit verifies the least-privilege desktop server contract.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

The minimal future server handoff should add a desktop device-authorization API namespace, place pending device and user codes in Redis with short TTL and one-time consumption, issue final credentials through existing NewAPI user_sessions, aggregate existing user, log, pricing, token and top-up data, and avoid new database schema unless deployment audit disproves the observed tag or an immutable billing field cannot fit existing JSON/options storage.
野菜API is an official desktop client whose first priority includes account access, balance, recharge, and usage visibility.
The current phase changes only the desktop client; NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration remain unchanged.
Desktop authorization is first-party authorization by the 野菜API website, not direct third-party provider login inside the client.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.
The desktop client compares the official-price baseline already configured in NewAPI with the current user's NewAPI price; it must not maintain a second independent numeric official-price table.

NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions are always maintained as the corresponding vendor official price; all 野菜API discounts are layered separately through user group ratios or explicit special billing rules.

The desktop account login uses first-party device authorization: the client opens the system browser for website login and explicit device approval, polls for completion, never places passwords, cookies, API keys, or final session credentials in the URL, handles cancellation and expiry explicitly, and supports website-side device revocation.

Desktop device authorization codes are single-use and expire after 10 minutes; access tokens last one hour and refresh automatically; the remembered device session expires after 30 days of inactivity and has a 90-day absolute reauthorization limit; logout, website revocation, and refresh failure are explicit invalidation paths, while sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.

The desktop account session uses least privilege: it may read the current account profile, balance, usage, available models, and prices and manage only the current device's per-tool relay keys and logout. Password, email, payment data, recharge records, user groups, other devices, other-device key plaintext, and administrative settings remain website-only or inaccessible.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner authorized the next client development unit for first-party website authorization, account balance and usage, recharge entry, and official-versus-actual price presentation while preserving the existing decision that NewAPI, servers, Nginx, and production configuration are not changed in the current phase.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.
Owner requests fixing mismatched native titlebar and confusing multiple Codex detection in installed beginner client.

decisions.question: What client-only successor release unit is authorized after RU-001 when the deployed NewAPI still lacks the approved desktop authorization boundary?
decisions.choice: Freeze RU-002 as a successor to RU-001. Preserve the branded five-tool read-only discovery experience and add the production account and billing information architecture, complete page states, fixed display-only 1 USD = 6.75 CNY context, and an updated future NewAPI change specification. The only runtime account projection in this unit is backend_upgrade_required: it performs no account network request, stores no credential, shows no fabricated account or numeric billing value, and exposes no active recharge or authorization action until a later frozen unit verifies a deployed least-privilege /api/desktop/v1 contract.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: How should the repaired client reach Apple Silicon and Windows internal testers, and what is the minimum future NewAPI persistence change?
decisions.choice: Create RU-018 as a packaging and handoff successor that depends on RU-017 without changing its runtime source. Build one signed and notarized universal macOS DMG with arm64 and x86_64 slices. Add a separate manual artifact-only Windows 2022 workflow for an unsigned NSIS internal installer in the private origin; do not use the inherited tag release workflow and do not publish a release or updater. For the server handoff, target deployed NewAPI v1.0.0-rc.27: reuse existing users, user_sessions, logs with Other JSON, tokens, pricing/options and top-up/payment records; keep pending device authorization codes in Redis with short TTL, one-time consumption and polling limits. Add no database schema by default. A later migration is allowed only if the server owner proves production schema drift or required immutable billing evidence cannot be retained in the existing JSON/options boundary. No server is changed in this unit.
decisions.decidedBy: implementation owner within explicit cross-platform build and server-analysis request

terms.definition: 由野菜API网站授权给桌面客户端、只用于账户和客户端管理接口的凭证状态。
依据当前用户、计费分组、模型、缓存、阶梯和价格版本计算的野菜API价格。
面向用户的 API 接入入口类别，例如大陆优化或全球线路；实际端点在高级信息中可见。
请求和本地工具配置中使用的真实模型标识，不得被推荐标签取代或隐藏。
模型厂商公开价格源在指定核对时间、单位和计费条件下声明的价格。
本地配置写入、读取回验和工具所需协议的最小连通性测试均成功后的状态。

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: RU-002 preserves RU-001 and adds a beginner-readable account and billing shell that truthfully reports the missing desktop backend boundary without contacting account services, storing credentials, fabricating values, or enabling recharge.
acceptance: The shell exposes clear Account and Local tools destinations and preserves the complete fixed five-tool read-only scan behavior from RU-001.
The account destination states that secure website authorization requires a future server upgrade and exposes no control that pretends authorization can currently begin or complete.
Balance, today usage, month usage, model ID, official price, actual price, and recharge remain visibly unavailable instead of showing zero, sample, cached, or inferred values.
The fixed 1 USD = 6.75 CNY comparison rate is labelled display-only and not presented as a live exchange rate or a billing input.

The runtime makes no account, pricing, usage, authorization, wallet, or other network request and persists no password, website cookie, access token, refresh token, API key, account profile, or scan history.

The updated future NewAPI specification is pinned to current official GitHub evidence, distinguishes current routes from proposed /api/desktop/v1 routes, and records the deployed 404 readiness result without changing NewAPI or production infrastructure.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: Repair native macOS titlebar consistency and automatically resolve standalone-versus-bundled CLI coexistence without asking beginners to choose paths.
acceptance: Transparent native titlebar and fixed light/dark background retain native decorations. Do not force application or OS appearance, so system mode stays automatic.

Version 2 deduplicates canonical aliases, excludes macOS .app internal executables before probing, selects only standalone candidate or unique earliest absolute PATH candidate. Ties and common-only ambiguity remain unresolved with desktop/retry actions. No user installation or configuration changes.

Fixed five-tool closed projection includes independent and bundled counts and selection reason. Only selected candidate probed; never fall back silently after failure. Reject stale/malformed responses. v1 stays unchanged.

Plain four-locale copy distinguishes Codex CLI. Test native selection, React/IPC theme ordering and scan transitions, workbench/cost regression and exact signed notarized local Intel package. No account, DSH, server, updater or public release activation.

requirements.statement: Package the verified repaired client for Apple Silicon capable macOS and unsigned Windows internal testing, while delivering a version-pinned NewAPI interface-versus-database handoff without changing any server or publishing a release.
acceptance: Build a Developer ID signed and notarized universal macOS application and DMG containing both arm64 and x86_64 executable slices. Exercise the Intel slice on this host and report that native Apple Silicon launch remains untested without an M-series host.

Use a separate manual private-repository Windows 2022 workflow that runs locked tests and builds only an unsigned internal NSIS installer, uploads a workflow artifact, and never creates a tag, release, updater artifact or public download.

Preserve the RU-017 runtime source and all account, DSH, credential, configuration-write, telemetry and updater boundaries; package evidence must bind every delivered artifact to source, architecture, signature state and hash.

Give the server owner a version-pinned endpoint and persistence matrix. Reuse NewAPI users, user_sessions, logs, tokens, pricing/options and top-up/payment records; use Redis only for expiring one-time device authorization state; add no new schema by default and name the exact audit condition that would justify a later migration.
Perform no server, NewAPI, Nginx, database, production, user-tool configuration or public-release mutation.

invariants: An account session is never projected into a third-party tool configuration.
Client cost calculations are estimates; the server billing ledger is authoritative.
V1 observes but does not install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
A desktop application observation is separate from a command-line executable observation and cannot prove login, configuration or end-to-end compatibility.
A diagnostic conclusion names only causes supported by collected evidence.
A configuration write cannot commit without an encrypted transaction-scoped rollback snapshot and external-change check; no successful transaction retains backup history.

contracts.authorization: Callable only by the bundled local shell. It grants no network, account, credential, wallet, payment, configuration, updater, telemetry, or server authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is a deterministic compiled-capability projection. Repeating it in RU-002 returns the same backend_upgrade_required truth except for the caller requestId.
contracts.compatibility: Version 1 has exactly one runtime status, backend_upgrade_required. A later deployed account integration requires a superseding contract and release unit rather than changing this meaning.

outputSchema.description: A fail-closed RU-002 projection that prevents unavailable remote capabilities from appearing live.

status.description: The only truthful account capability state in RU-002.

networkAttempted.description: Whether this projection attempted any account network request.

serverNamespace.description: The future first-party namespace required before activation.

authorization.description: Whether website device authorization is available in this client-only unit.

accountSummary.description: Whether real account balance and summary data is available.

usage.description: Whether real account usage data is available.

pricing.description: Whether a server-authoritative official-versus-actual price projection is available.

recharge.description: Whether a verified first-party recharge destination is available.

comparisonFx.description: Product-approved display context that is not a live rate or billing input.

usdToCny.description: The product-approved fixed USD-to-CNY comparison display rate.

purpose.description: The sole permitted purpose of the fixed rate.

liveRate.description: Whether the fixed display rate is a live market exchange rate.

observability.correlation: requestId exists only in transient local UI state.
observability.audit: RU-002 creates no account or authorization audit record because it performs no remote or persistent account operation.
observability.metrics: RU-002 records and uploads no account, billing, or readiness metric.

errorSemantics: The projection never falls back to browser cookies, browser access tokens, a manually pasted PAT, generic NewAPI token CRUD, or public pricing interpretation.
Unavailable balance, usage, price, model, and wallet data are represented as unavailable rather than zero or stale values.
A future server becoming reachable does not silently activate RU-002; activation requires a superseding frozen contract and executable deployed integration evidence.

contracts.authorization: Bundled main window only. Fixed background palette; no arbitrary colors/windows, filesystem, credentials, network or OS preference authority.
contracts.idempotency: Same fixed palette is idempotent. Renderer serializes/coalesces calls; native acknowledges assignment on main thread. Transient presentation only; no canonical resource write or domain event.
contracts.compatibility: Native decorations and OS appearance retained. CSS owns web content; native Window background only. Browser preview skips native call.

outputSchema.description: Assignment acknowledged, not a paint guarantee.

errorSemantics: Reject non-main caller or unknown theme before assignment.
Catch native failure without business side effects; next update retries. System matchMedia remains untouched.

contracts.authorization: Callable only by the bundled local desktop webview; it grants no account, credential, filesystem-write, installation, update, or network authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is read-only. Repeating one request against the same executable paths yields an equivalent projection; the UI accepts results only for its newest requestId.
contracts.compatibility: Active renderer uses new v2 command; v1 unchanged. All versions remain unverified read-only.

requestId.description: Caller-generated correlation identifier used to reject stale UI results.

outputSchema.description: The complete bounded projection for the five V1 tools.

platform.description: The platform family on which discovery ran.

startedAtEpochMs.description: Local monotonic correlation timestamp expressed as Unix milliseconds for freshness display.

completedAtEpochMs.description: Completion timestamp expressed as Unix milliseconds and never earlier than startedAtEpochMs.

tools.description: Exactly one result for every V1 tool in stable product order.

status.description: Observed installation and executable outcome without inferred configuration health.

version.description: Exact normalized version output when available, otherwise an empty string.

candidateCount.description: Distinct standalone executables only; aliases deduplicated, max 32. Reaching bound forces unresolved.

locationHint.description: A sanitized source hint such as PATH or common location, never a complete user path or OS username.

compatibility.description: Conservative automatic-configuration eligibility for this release unit.

reasonCode.description: Stable presentation reason with no raw command output or secret-bearing diagnostic text.

bundledCount.description: Ignored deduplicated macOS app-internal components, capped at 32.

selection.description: Read-only probe resolution, never configuration authority.

observability.correlation: requestId is returned unchanged and shown in advanced local details only.
observability.audit: RU-001 emits no persistent audit record; the current in-memory result is the sole local projection.
observability.metrics: RU-001 sends no telemetry and records no persistent metrics; elapsed time is computed in memory for the current scan only.

errorSemantics: Validate request before discovery; never expose complete paths or raw diagnostic output.
Absolute PATH/common directories only; canonical deduplication; macOS .app/Contents/{MacOS,Resources,Frameworks,Helpers} entries or canonical targets are bundled and never probed.
One standalone auto-selects; multiple select unique lowest absolute PATH rank. Equal rank, common-only ambiguity or candidate bound remains unresolved, not probed.

Zero standalone is not_found; bundled_only explains desktop component. Selected probe failure/timeout never switches target; only sanitized numeric semantic-style version returned, otherwise probe_failed.
UI enforces closed projection and newest correlation; stale or malformed results cannot enable capabilities.

default.behavior: Show the account and billing composition with one clear backend-upgrade-required notice and unavailable placeholders for every remote fact.
default.visibleTruth: The secure first-party desktop authorization interface is not deployed, so no account, balance, usage, price, model, or wallet fact has been requested.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim that login, account data, billing data, or recharge is available, and do not show zero or sample numbers.
default.freshness: No remote freshness timestamp exists in RU-002.
default.recovery: A later verified server integration release replaces this projection; the user cannot repair the missing backend from the client.
default.correlation: A transient local requestId identifies only the deterministic readiness projection.

loading.behavior: Reserve a clear skeleton for a future newest account request while hiding all prior numeric values from the active result.
loading.visibleTruth: A future integration may be checking current account data; RU-002 itself never enters this network state.
prohibitedClaims: Do not keep an old balance or price visually current while a newer request is unresolved.
loading.freshness: Only the newest future requestId may produce current data.
loading.recovery: A failed future request transitions to error without inventing completion.
loading.correlation: Future loading belongs to exactly one requestId.

empty.behavior: Explain that an authorized future account returned no usage or comparable pricing rows while keeping the known account state separate.
empty.visibleTruth: The server returned a successful but empty projection for the selected range.
prohibitedClaims: Do not convert missing usage or price rows into a zero-cost or free-service claim.
empty.freshness: Show the server data timestamp and selected range.
empty.recovery: The user may retry or select another range after the future contract is active.
empty.correlation: The empty result remains bound to its server requestId and data timestamp.

partial.behavior: Show each available future projection independently and mark unavailable balance, usage, pricing, or wallet data by name.
partial.visibleTruth: Only the named server projections completed successfully.
prohibitedClaims: Do not derive a missing official price from an actual price or a missing balance from cached usage.
partial.freshness: Each future projection shows its own server timestamp and pricing version where applicable.
partial.recovery: Retry only the missing projection without erasing truthful completed sections.
partial.correlation: Each partial section retains its originating requestId.

error.behavior: Show a stable safe error class and hide unverified numeric account and billing values.
error.visibleTruth: The newest future account request did not produce a valid projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not parse a server message into a guessed balance, price, authorization, or payment state.
error.freshness: Any prior data is visibly expired and cannot be presented as current.
error.recovery: Retry creates a new requestId; authentication failures require the explicit authorization recovery path.
error.correlation: Only safe request and error codes may be shown; secrets and raw server bodies remain hidden.

expired.behavior: Replace account facts with an expired-session notice and remove active wallet and billing actions.
expired.visibleTruth: The future desktop session or data freshness window has expired and current account truth is unavailable.
prohibitedClaims: Do not keep cached account, price, usage, or wallet data looking live.
expired.freshness: Expired data keeps only a visible stale timestamp if retained in memory for explanation.
expired.recovery: Reauthorize through the system browser after the future server contract is active.
expired.correlation: The expired device session ID is never displayed or logged.

conflict.behavior: Explain a future authorization replay, already-used code, device revocation, or newest-request conflict without choosing a successful state.
conflict.visibleTruth: The server rejected the operation because the device authorization or session identity no longer owns the expected state.
prohibitedClaims: Do not treat an already-used or mismatched authorization as approved.
conflict.freshness: Conflicted credentials and results are immediately ineligible for current display.
conflict.recovery: Start a new single-use authorization request in a future integrated release.
conflict.correlation: The user sees a safe conflict code and support requestId only.

recovery.behavior: Show the exact safe next step for backend unavailable, network retry, expired session, rejection, or revocation.
recovery.visibleTruth: Recovery has not completed until the corresponding future server response succeeds.
prohibitedClaims: Do not auto-authorize, auto-recharge, or silently fall back to broad website credentials.
recovery.freshness: Recovery starts a new request identity and invalidates superseded results.
recovery.recovery: Follow only the action allowed by the stable server error code; RU-002 exposes only the server-requirements explanation.
recovery.correlation: Every future recovery attempt receives a new requestId.

processing.behavior: Reserve a waiting-for-browser-approval state that shows the non-secret user code and expiry only after the future device authorization contract exists.
processing.visibleTruth: A future device authorization may be pending, denied, approved, cancelled, expired, or slowed down; RU-002 never fabricates one.
prohibitedClaims: Do not put passwords, cookies, access tokens, refresh tokens, API keys, or final session credentials in a URL or visible code.
processing.freshness: The future server-provided expiry owns the pending state and cannot be extended by the client.
processing.recovery: Cancellation or expiry requires a new authorization request; slow_down obeys the server interval.
processing.correlation: Only the authorization requestId and non-secret user code may be presented.

default.behavior: Show the 野菜API welcome shell, the fixed five-tool list, and one primary button labelled to check installed tools.
default.visibleTruth: No discovery result exists yet; the page says that the check is local and read-only and that no API knowledge is required.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim that any tool is installed, configured, compatible, connected, or ready before a scan result exists.
default.freshness: No result timestamp is shown before the first scan.
default.recovery: The user may start the local scan or close the app without changing the machine.
default.correlation: A requestId is generated only when the user starts a scan.

loading.behavior: Keep all five tool cards visible with per-tool checking indicators and disable duplicate scan submission while the current request is active.
loading.visibleTruth: The page says that local executables and their version output are being checked and that no configuration or network action is running.
prohibitedClaims: Do not show cached installation or compatibility results as the active scan result.
loading.freshness: The active requestId and start time own the pending result.
loading.recovery: If the request fails, transition to error while retaining no invented tool status.
loading.correlation: Only the active requestId may complete this state.

empty.behavior: Show all five tools as not found and explain that this is not an application error.
empty.visibleTruth: The most recent completed local scan found no executable candidate for any supported tool.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim the tools are uninstalled when they may exist outside the bounded discovery locations.
empty.freshness: Show the completion time of the newest accepted requestId.
empty.recovery: The user may install a tool independently and rescan; RU-001 never installs it.
empty.correlation: Advanced details show the newest accepted requestId without a complete local path.

partial.behavior: Show each of the five tool results independently so found, not-found, failed, timed-out, and read-only states can coexist.
partial.visibleTruth: Only observations from the newest completed local scan appear, including exact version text for successful probes.
prohibitedClaims: Do not promote one tool's success into a claim about another tool or about configuration health.
partial.freshness: All cards share the newest accepted scan completion time.
partial.recovery: A failed or missing tool can be rescanned without hiding valid results for the other tools.
partial.correlation: Every visible card belongs to the same newest requestId.

error.behavior: Show a plain-language scan failure without replacing it with guessed installation results.
error.visibleTruth: The discovery query did not produce a valid complete five-tool projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not display the previous scan as if it were the failed request's current result.
error.freshness: The failed requestId is identified and prior results are visibly stale or cleared.
error.recovery: Retry creates a new requestId and performs the same bounded read-only scan.
error.correlation: The safe local error class is correlated to the failed requestId; raw command output is not displayed.

expired.behavior: Mark a superseded result as expired and prevent it from overwriting a newer request.
expired.visibleTruth: A scan completion arrived for an older requestId and was rejected from the current projection.
prohibitedClaims: Do not merge cards from different request identities or completion times.
expired.freshness: Only the newest started requestId is eligible to become current.
expired.recovery: Continue showing the newest active or completed request; no filesystem recovery is required.
expired.correlation: Both expired and current request identities remain in transient UI control flow only.

conflict.behavior: Highlight every tool with multiple canonical executable candidates and explain that no candidate was silently chosen.
conflict.visibleTruth: The bounded scan observed more than one distinct executable for at least one tool.
prohibitedClaims: Do not claim compatibility, choose a preferred executable, or expose a configure action while installation identity is ambiguous.
conflict.freshness: Candidate counts come only from the newest accepted scan.
conflict.recovery: The user resolves the tool installation externally, then rescans; RU-001 changes no PATH or tool file.
conflict.correlation: The conflict and sanitized candidate source classes are bound to one requestId.

recovery.behavior: After a failed, timed-out, or superseded scan, explain that a clean rescan is the only in-app recovery action.
recovery.visibleTruth: No write or rollback is necessary because discovery is read-only and stores no retained scan history.
prohibitedClaims: Do not offer repair, install, update, configuration, credential, or restore operations in RU-001.
recovery.freshness: Recovery always creates a new requestId and never mutates an older result.
recovery.recovery: Run another bounded local scan; if it fails again, preserve the truthful per-tool failure states.
recovery.correlation: The recovery request receives its own requestId.

processing.behavior: Represent each bounded version probe as in progress while keeping configuration and remote-service controls absent.
processing.visibleTruth: Only local executable discovery and a bounded --version command may be processing.
prohibitedClaims: Do not imply that login, billing, API connectivity, model retrieval, updates, or configuration are processing.
processing.freshness: Processing belongs to the newest active requestId and expires when it is superseded.
processing.recovery: Each probe times out into a truthful per-tool result; the overall projection still completes when possible.
processing.correlation: Per-tool processing is aggregated under one requestId without persistent telemetry.

packages.objective: Package the unchanged RU-017 client for universal macOS and unsigned Windows internal testing, and hand off the minimal NewAPI API/persistence boundary.
deliverables: Developer ID signed and notarized universal macOS app and DMG with verified arm64 and x86_64 slices, exact hash and honest host-test boundary.
Manual private-repository Windows 2022 internal workflow and downloaded unsigned NSIS artifact with exact hash and SmartScreen limitation.
Version-pinned server-owner handoff distinguishing reusable NewAPI records and APIs, Redis-only transient state, and the evidence threshold for any later schema migration.
nonGoals: No renderer or Rust runtime behavior changes, server/NewAPI/Nginx/database changes, user tool writes, DSH activation, account activation or credential access.
No Windows code-signing claim, Apple Silicon native launch claim, tag, GitHub Release, updater artifact, public download or full-product readiness claim.
No inherited broad upstream release workflow execution.
allowedPaths: outputs/野菜API-跨平台内测构建与后端边界记录.md

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No client or server data migration. Server schema advice is documentation only and defaults to no new schema on deployed NewAPI v1.0.0-rc.27.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Retain RU-017 Intel artifact; remove only RU-018 local artifacts and the isolated internal workflow if requested.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Package the exact RU-017 runtime for additional operating-system architectures without changing its contracts.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: macOS universal internal build; Windows x64 unsigned NSIS internal build; NewAPI handoff pinned to v1.0.0-rc.27.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Public distribution, updater enablement, Windows signing or server activation requires a later decision, evidence and freeze.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Windows internal workflow is manual, x64 Windows 2022, locked, artifact-only and contains no release, updater or signing path.
Backend handoff reuses deployed NewAPI persistence, scopes Redis device authorization safely and makes every future schema condition explicit.
Delivered universal macOS and Windows internal artifacts have exact architecture, signature/state, source and hash evidence without overstated platform validation.

stopConditions: A runtime source, server, database, public release, updater or user-machine configuration change is required.
Apple signing/notarization cannot use the existing authorized identity/profile or Windows build would require a secret/signing claim.
A delivered artifact cannot be bound to the exact source and verification receipt.
